imports:
import BanditRLProof.OnlineSubgradientBasic

/-!
# Absolute-value subdifferential
Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization,
arXiv:1912.13213v10, Example 2.24, printed page 18 / PDF page 30.
These equalities characterize every global scalar support: positive queries
have slope 1, zero admits the entire closed interval [-1,1], and negative
queries have slope -1. Real-valued absolute value is embedded into EReal only
to reuse the shared support definition. This is not a higher-dimensional norm
claim, an algorithm guarantee, Chapter 2 completion, or whole-book completion.
-/
scope: noncomputable section; open Set; namespace BanditRL.OnlineConvex
space: ALL four public proofs specialize to scalar ℝ; no E/FiniteDimensional/CompleteSpace explicit binder
borrowed_definition:
def SourceSubdifferential (f : E → EReal) (x : E) : Set E :=
  {g | ∀ y, f x + (inner ℝ g (y - x) : EReal) ≤ f y}
generic_scope_delta: S permits all EReal functions, broader than printed proper-function definition; fixed real-valued absolute function is finite/proper at every x so this source instance is legitimate.
